messages:
elaine: kicking off the penetration engagement thread — quick Qs before we hand over access to the assessors. scope: staging only, no prod creds. timeline: target window next Wed 09:00-17:00 PT. main asks: log retention for evidence, how we hand over KMS-wrapped secrets for readroom, and any RBAC changes needed for ephemeral access.

matt: thanks. for logs we usually snapshot 30 days by default but we can extend to 90 for this engagement. do you want full request+response body capture or headers+metadata only? :thinking_face: 

elaine: need full request bodies for the assessor proofing but sanitize PII. retention 90d sounds right. also need presigned S3 readroom access or a temporary bucket?

samir: presigned S3 is fine. we should use a timeboxed prefix and object lock disabled for the window. plan: upload artifacts to s3://redwood-pt-readroom/<eng-id>/ then rotate creds. I'll generate presigned URLs with 48h TTL and a single-download policy for large bundles.

jordan: for KMS: we should avoid handing over customer master key material. we can create a dedicated KMS key (alias/pt-eng-2026-<eng-id>) with decrypt-only policy for a service principal that runs the evidence packager. after packaging we wrap artifacts with that key and upload. Assessors won't get the key — we give them presigned URLs to the wrapped objects and a short-lived unwrap token via the readroom runner.

elaine: ok good. what about RBAC? we need least-privilege but also the assessor must be able to query CloudWatch logs + tracing.

ryan: create two ephemeral roles: pt-assessor-read (CloudWatchReadOnly, X-RayRead) and pt-assessor-s3 (s3:GetObject on the readroom prefix). roles should be assumable only from the assessor IP ranges and require MFA session tags. I can craft the trust policy.

matt: small note: CloudWatch Insights queries are rate-limited. recommend pre-slicing logs into the evidence bundle for heavy queries so assessors don't blow quotas during the window. also enable metric filters for any anomaly signals we expect them to validate.

elaine: thanks. incident/cookie-cutter: if they trigger an accidental alert or high-sev vuln, do we pause the window or continue with mitigations? what's the playbook?

samir: we treat accidental destructive actions as live-fire — immediately pause and notify oncall, take snapshots, preserve evidence. for high-sev vulns that could impact other tenants we stop and escalate. I'll add a short runbook snippet to the engagement doc.

sec-oncall-bot: @oncall paging policy: if an assessor action causes a system outage >5m, escalate to oncall rotation. See: https://redwood.internal/oncall/policy

elaine: actionable next steps: 1) ryan to post trust policy + role ARNs by EOD, 2) samir to prep packaging script + presigned URL process, 3) matt to slice logs for heavy queries and list metric filters, 4) sec-oncall-bot link will be added to readroom. I'll confirm retest slot after we verify artifacts uploaded.

ryan: got it, posting trust policy now. will include IP ranges and MFA tag example.

samir: packaging script example for auditors (will sanitize PII):
```bash
./package_evidence.sh --eng-id ENG-472 --start 2026-02-10T08:00Z --end 2026-02-10T16:00Z \\n  --include-logs request_bodies --sanitize-rules rules.json \\n  --kms-alias alias/pt-eng-2026-ENG-472 \
  --upload-bucket redwood-pt-readroom
```

matt: LGTM. small ask: can we set S3 bucket to log-access to a separate audit bucket so we have an immutable audit record of downloads?

samir: yes — enable server access logs and CloudTrail data events for s3:GetObject on the readroom prefix. we'll export to audit-bucket with lifecycle 365d.

elaine: perfect. last item: retest coordination — I'll open a separate thread to book next-week retest slot after the remediation PRs land. for this thread, recording acceptance criteria: artifacts uploaded + roles created + KMS alias created + 90d retention + audit logging enabled.

jordan: noted. I'll sign-off on KMS policy once samir attaches the wrapping key ARN.

elaine: thanks all — feel free to ping me if anything slips. :thumbsup:
